# Contributing

Read the project's own page. Write the entry from that page.

## Submit

1. Open this repository on GitHub.
2. Click **Issues**.
3. Click **New issue**.
4. Next to **Contribution**, click **Get started**.
5. Fill the form from the project's own page.
6. Click **Submit new issue**.

To change the README yourself: open **README.md**, click the pencil, edit, click **Commit changes**, then click **Commit changes** again in the dialog. If GitHub asks you to fork first, click **Fork this repository**, finish the edit, click **Propose changes**, then click **Create pull request**.

## Entry

```markdown
## Name

Two or three sentences. The name stays plain text.

- Repository: [https://github.com/org/repo](https://github.com/org/repo)

> [!NOTE]
> Click below to see more details.

<details>
<summary>More details</summary>

License, last push, stars, and one row per category.
The wording is the project's. Tag it `README`, `Docs`, or `Site`.

</details>
```

Skip the repository line when there is no public repo, and put the vendor page in More details. Other links stay in More details. Leave a blank line after `<summary>`.

## Where

- A public repository: `# Open Source`. NukeRat stays first. Havoc stays directly under Sliver.
- Vendor page, no public repo: `# Commercial`.

Do not add install commands, operating steps, or a category the page does not state.

List text is [CC0](../LICENSE).
